findings.body:
**Install the rendered fleet-reader plist, and make it run the script that the runbook installs.**

The plist runs `@CRQ_ROOT@/ops/fleet-reader.py` (line 8). That path is not the Application Support copy that the cutover runbook installs. The runbook copies the script to `~/Library/Application Support/crq/fleet-reader.py` and copies the plist to `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`, then bootstraps it. The loaded job does not run the Application Support copy. It runs the path at line 8.

Two outcomes follow, depending on how the plist is copied:

- If the template is copied without rendering, `@CRQ_ROOT@` stays literal. launchd cannot start the job, and the fleet reader does not run.
- If the rendered plist is copied, the job runs the checkout script at `<runner root>/apps/crq-python/ops/fleet-reader.py`. It does not run the copy in Application Support. The job then depends on that checkout existing on worker-host and on its version. An update to the Application Support copy has no effect.

Make the installed plist and the installed script refer to the same location. Render the plist before installation. Confirm that the checkout path or the Application Support path, as chosen, exists and is current on worker-host.
findings.title: Install the rendered fleet-reader plist, and make it run the script that the runbook installs.

findings.body:
**Set `XDG_STATE_HOME` for the launchd watchdog to match the runner.**

`com.crq.watchdog.plist:9` sets only `PATH` and `HOME`. launchd does not pass a login shell's environment to a job, so a custom `XDG_STATE_HOME` that the runner uses is absent here. `crq-watchdog.py:9-10` then reads `heartbeat.json` from `~/.local/state/crq`. The runner writes to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/crq` (`crq.py:3870-3883`). With a non-default value, the two paths differ.

If the default file is absent, `crq-watchdog.py:29` raises `FileNotFoundError`. Nothing catches it, so the run exits 1 with no stall alert. If a stale default file exists, the watchdog can alert on old data.

The install step that renders this plist should set `XDG_STATE_HOME` to the value the runner uses. Alternatively, both sides can use one fixed heartbeat path. The choice between these is open and should be made by the maintainers.
findings.title: Set `XDGSTATEHOME` for the launchd watchdog to match the runner.
